problems.label: Physical symptoms that take over daily life
definitions: Has physical symptoms such as pain or fatigue on most days that cause real distress.
Spends much of the day attending to, researching or worrying about the symptoms.
Has cut back on work, social life or activities because of the symptoms.
longTermGoals: The client lives a fuller life alongside the symptoms, with steady activity, less worry and consistent medical care.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 4 weeks, agree on a consistent plan with one medical clinician, including scheduled check-ups.
Plan daily activity at a steady level and increase it by small steps each week, logged for 6 weeks.
By session 6, name 3 valued activities and do at least one of them each week, whatever the symptom level.
Practice a 5-minute attention shift or mindfulness exercise daily and rate symptom distress before and after.
Complete the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and every 4 weeks; if low mood or worry is high, discuss a medication evaluation.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
